NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI computing value chain, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that is critically dependent on TSMC's advanced packaging and leading-edge nodes (CoWoS, 4nm) and HBM memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Micron) for its H100/Blackwell GPU platforms. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is increasingly concentrated among a handful of hyperscale cloud providers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle) who are racing to build AI infrastructure, making NVIDIA's fortunes tightly coupled to hyperscaler capital expenditure cycles.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the premium consumer-facing end of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as the chief architect and systems integrator while outsourcing fabrication to partners like TSMC and Samsung for its custom silicon and displays. Its downstream relationships span global telecom carriers, major retailers, and platform partners whose ecosystems and distribution channels are critical to sustaining Apple's industry-leading volumes and high-margin Services revenue.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor supply chain as a vertically integrated memory manufacturer, heavily dependent on a small set of specialized capital equipment suppliers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its multi-billion dollar fab capex program. On the demand side, Micron serves a concentrated base of hyperscalers, AI chip designers, and OEMs, with NVIDIA's surging HBM demand and cloud capex cycles being the most significant near-term revenue drivers.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings sits at the apex of the semiconductor IP ecosystem, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chip designer globally rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making its upstream dependencies primarily software tools (EDA) and cloud services rather than physical materials. Its downstream relationships span the entire semiconductor value chain — from mobile SoC designers like Qualcomm and MediaTek, to hyperscalers like Apple and Amazon building custom silicon, giving ARM extraordinary leverage but also high customer concentration risk with Apple alone representing roughly 25% of royalty and licensing revenue.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at the intersection of fabless semiconductor design and hyperscale cloud infrastructure, acting as a critical supplier of custom ASICs, Ethernet networking silicon, and storage controllers to the world's largest data center operators and networking OEMs. The company is heavily dependent on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing and ARM for processor IP, while its revenue growth is increasingly tied to the AI-driven capital expenditure cycles of major cloud hyperscalers like AWS, Google, and Microsoft.
